The monitoring results we have seen from Helen Keller are less comprehensive than those from GiveWell’s other top charities. We have seen monitoring results for campaigns representing 64% of Helen Keller’s VAS spending in 2019, 52% in 2020 and 29% in 2021. In part, our understanding is that this fall has been because of temporary disruption resulting from the coronavirus pandemic. For more information, see our monitoring analysis here: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Jo0ZnCNLljWVnmwngaCnXex3aZNyYqWli1P29PTfJ58/edit#gid=389966275

We also have a concern that the monitoring results we see may not be fully reflective of the results achieved across Helen Keller’s VAS campaigns. That is because Helen Keller usually conducts monitoring for only one of the two campaign rounds it delivers per country per year, and in some cases only some regions or districts are surveyed. Overall, we believe that Helen Keller's coverage surveys are designed to measure key indicators of the success of VAS campaigns and to achieve samples that are generally representative of target populations. Helen Keller’s surveys use an audit procedure whereby supervisors re-survey a random sample of participants, and Helen Keller has increasingly begun to report the results from this procedure. This alleviates some of our initial concerns about the quality of Helen Keller's auditing procedure and gives us more confidence in the accuracy of the monitoring data. However, we note that the caregiver-reported nature of responses may produce bias in results. 

For more information on our analysis of Helen Keller’s monitoring, see our grantee review here: https://www.givewell.org/charities/helen-keller-international#Methodology/

rows.label: Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
